solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minister ended with other ranks

parts.note: something ended is over and done, in the past
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A clergyman's service came to an end in the company of the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion in charge of a congregation is a pastor; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Top co-eds fuelled by such a lottery?

indicators.note: fuelled, as if tanked up on drink, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leading female students are the driving force behind a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A postcode lottery is a British phrase for services that vary arbitrarily by where you live.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcode lottery, in British usage, is unequal provision that depends on one's address.

clue.text: Drama somehow appears — old and ordinary within

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A play somehow seems both dated and run of the mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' says the two Os go inside the jumbled letters of 'appears'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serialised television or radio drama about everyday lives.

clue.text: Cooker has one almost complete and new

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: something complete is finished, or over

explanation.surface: The kitchen has a nearly finished, brand-new range installed.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed heated compartment in which food is cooked.

clue.text: Hissing letter included in huge gifts given generously

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, so the letter's name sits within the word for huge

parts.note: huge means large
the letter S makes a hissing sound; its name is spelt ESS

explanation.surface: A sibilant character is part of some enormous presents handed out freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hissing letter' describes S by its sound; the solver must spell its name out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, or the money and presents bestowed by a benefactor.

clue.text: Secured date ain't flexible

indicators.note: a flexible arrangement can be bent into other forms, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The date is fixed and won't be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Attained means achieved or gained, a synonym of having secured something.

clue.text: Glad after toddling around new place to live

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for new
toddling, walking unsteadily like an infant, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Happy once the toddler wanders round the new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toddling' rearranges GLAD AFTER into GARDEFLAT; 'around' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flat is a ground-floor apartment with access to a garden, a kind of home.

clue.text: Soldier's cap is small, hard and a knockout

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear is compact and tough, and looks stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military hat with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Software designer, say, rejecting first three finds loving runaway?

indicators.note: the first three letters of the word are thrown away

parts.note: a software designer is an example of a developer

explanation.surface: A programmer turns down three suitors and runs off to marry for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who elopes runs away secretly to marry, a lover fleeing to wed.

clue.text: Stocking material in name only, strangely

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Hosiery labelled as a fabric in name only, which seems odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is the synthetic fibre from which stockings are commonly made.

clue.text: Showing great dignity art gallery cut cunning

indicators.note: the gallery's name cuts into the word for cunning, splitting it open

parts.note: cunning means sly
the Tate is the famous art gallery in London

explanation.surface: Someone at a gallery, cutting a dignified figure, is also crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of national art galleries in Britain, best known for Tate Britain and Tate Modern in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately describes something majestic and dignified in bearing, like a slow formal procession.

clue.text: Bother chasing rent could be a big blow

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the word for bother follows the word for rent

parts.note: rent, as a past participle of rend, means torn
bother or fuss is ado

explanation.surface: Fuss over the landlord's rent demand could turn into a big blow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but here it means ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, an example of a very strong blow of wind.

clue.text: Fool caught by destiny

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: An idiot was trapped by fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid or clumsy person, an idiot.

clue.text: Phone in caravan, perhaps

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: Making a call from inside a caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is one example of a dwelling on wheels that can be moved from place to place.

clue.text: Choose haphazardly, let in last of workforce — not across this!

parts.note: to choose is to pick

indicators.note: haphazardly means in a random order, so the letters are scrambled
the last letter of the word workforce is taken

explanation.surface: Pick at random and let in the final worker, but don't cross this!
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' turns LET IN into ETLIN. Striking workers urge others not to cross their line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of striking workers is something colleagues are urged not to cross.

clue.text: Female deer with deadly greed kills

parts.note: a female deer is a doe
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A doe with a murderous appetite slaughters.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in is an idiom meaning to murder them.

clue.text: Mean what seafood stall may do? Only one line

indicators.note: of the two Ls in the phrase, only one is kept, so one of them goes

parts.note: a seafood stall would sell fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's stall appears, with a hint about a single line of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only one line' means the double L of SELL FISH is cut to one. 'Mean' is an adjective here, ungenerous, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean, in the sense of stingy and unwilling to share, is a synonym of self-centred greed.

clue.text: Sun god — it almost voiced patience

parts.note: Sol is the Roman sun god

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an opinion voiced is aired

explanation.surface: A sun god nearly spoke up about his patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the British name for the single-player card game known in the US as solitaire.

clue.text: Warning on valley: retweet

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a dale is a valley
RT is the social-media abbreviation for retweet

explanation.surface: Someone retweets an alert about a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of warning of imminent danger.

clue.text: Start to pick off what Scouts cook on?

definitions.meaning: to start shooting at targets, picking them off one by one
Scouts camping cook over a campfire in the open

explanation.surface: Scouts begin choosing what to cook their food on.
explanation.definitionFit: Open fire is both a command to begin shooting and a fire burning in the open air.

clue.text: Coach from London borough

definitions.meaning: a horse-drawn carriage for hire was a ... carriage

explanation.surface: A coach company comes from a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney names both a hired horse-drawn carriage and a borough in east London.

clue.text: Career in brass work

parts.note: brass in the sense of cheek or nerve is gall
OP is the abbreviation of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A career spent working in brass, such as a metalworker or bandsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb here: to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at high speed, as a horse at full stretch does.

clue.text: Appliance's ring which keeps joints together

definitions.meaning: a washing machine, the household appliance, is also called this
a flat ring placed under a nut or bolt to make a tight joint

explanation.surface: A machine has a ring holding its joints together.
explanation.definitionFit: Washer means both a washing machine and the flat ring that seals a bolted joint.

clue.text: André has one charming accent

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
charming means cute

explanation.surface: A man named André has a delightful way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'André has' sets the scene: the final é of André carries this very accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the accent sloping upward to the right, as over the e in café.

clue.text: Right of entry at Camden, it changed

indicators.note: the letters of these words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Access rules at Camden, a London district, have been altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is permission or the right to enter a place.

clue.text: What starts concert I reckon up in score?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to reckon is to add up, or sum

indicators.note: what starts the word concert is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musician asks what opens a concert, reckoning it must be in the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written notation of a piece of music for performers.

clue.text: Bowl over small barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: Knock over a little cask, like a bowling game at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl over' looks literal, but means to astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to amaze or stagger them, which is a synonym of stun.

clue.text: Passing cheese endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: something passing is short-lived, or brief

explanation.surface: A fleeting taste of cheese that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft creamy French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Sadly hotel is unfriendly

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are badly or wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A traveller regrets that the hotel's welcome is cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means antagonistic or unfriendly toward someone.

clue.text: Training stops with these finally

parts.note: read as train-ing, a journey by rail ends at the last stations of the line

explanation.surface: A coach says the exercise session ends with these last few drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like exercise but splits as a rail journey, which stops at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway stations at the end of a line, where trains finally halt, are known by this plural.

clue.text: Once more make tree (Acer) flourishing

indicators.note: flourishing suggests the letters are waved about into a new shape

explanation.surface: A gardener wants to grow another thriving maple tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Acer is the botanical name for the maple.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate is to produce or build something again, making it a second time.

clue.text: Harsh hack back in vogue

parts.note: to hack off is to cut, or sever

indicators.note: the back of the word vogue is its final letter

explanation.surface: Brutal, chopped hairstyles are fashionable once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in vogue' looks like 'fashionable again', but 'back in' picks the last letter of vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and harsh are synonyms, describing strict or unsparing treatment.
